Play & Party Hire

Kids party hire, sized to the space you actually have

Seven kinds of play and party hire, all delivered, set up and packed down. The right one depends on two things you can measure before you enquire. The age of the children and the flat ground you have.

Delivered and set upAges 1 to 13Indoor and outdoor
Get free quotes Find my area

Play hire works differently from entertainment. Nobody performs, nobody needs the room to be quiet, and the hire window usually covers the whole party rather than an hour of it. That makes it the better value option for the ages a performer cannot hold, and a useful backdrop for the ages who can be held.

The constraint is physical rather than social. Every item on this page has a footprint, a clearance requirement and a surface it can or cannot be installed on. A castle that will not fit through your side gate is not a cheaper castle, it is no castle at all.

Measure the flat area, measure the narrowest point of your access, and note the surface. Those three numbers make every quote you receive accurate.

Before you enquire

Three measurements that make every quote accurate

Five minutes with a tape measure prevents the most common problem in play hire, which is a delivery that cannot be installed.

The flat area, in metres. Not the block size. The genuinely flat, clear rectangle you can give them, and remember operators want about a metre of clearance on every side.
The narrowest point of the access path. Usually a side gate. Rolled castles and soft play panels are bulky, and this is where more deliveries fail than anywhere else.
The surface, and any slope. Grass, pavers, concrete, decking, tiles or carpet. Slope matters as much as surface, because operators will decline a noticeable one.

Common questions

Kids party hire questions

What is the difference between soft play and a jumping castle?

Soft play is a padded, ground level play area for babies through to about five. A jumping castle is an inflatable needing power, anchoring and open ground, suited to about three and up. Parties with a wide age range often book both in separate zones.

Is delivery and setup included?

Almost always for play hire. Delivery, setup, pack down and collection are normally in the price, with the hire window typically running three to four hours. Confirm the delivery and collection times when you book, because they are the detail that most often slips.

Can play hire be set up indoors?

Soft play, ball pits and toddler play generally can, on most flooring. Inflatables usually cannot, because of ceiling height and anchoring. If the forecast is uncertain, an indoor capable option removes the risk entirely.

Is supervision included with play hire?

No. Play hire is equipment, not supervision. An adult needs to be watching the area for the full hire, and every operator says the same in their terms. Some castle operators offer a supervising attendant at extra cost.

How far ahead should I book play hire?

Four to six weeks for most weekends and longer through the October to March peak. Soft play and castles are the two items that book out first on a Saturday morning.
